title: At the Supermarket
summary: Shopping for food — countable/uncountable nouns, prices, some/any.
text:
It is Saturday morning. Omar goes to the supermarket near his flat. He takes a list from his pocket. On the list there are five things: milk, eggs, rice, apples and soap.

First he goes to the fruit section. The apples are cheap today, so he takes six. Then he looks for milk. There is no milk on the shelf. Omar asks a worker: "Excuse me, do you have any milk?" The worker says, "Yes, we have some in the back. One moment, please."

Omar waits two minutes. The worker comes back with two bottles of milk. Omar says thank you and puts one bottle in his basket.

At the checkout, the total is fourteen dollars and twenty cents. Omar pays with his card. The cashier gives him a receipt. "Do you need a bag?" she asks. "No, thank you," says Omar. He has a bag in his backpack. He always brings his own bag because plastic bags are bad for the planet.

questions.q: How many things are on Omar's list?
Why does Omar take six apples?
Where is the milk at first?
Why does Omar say no to a bag?
